evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 形義通解; components, proposals and attestations
evidence.text: The entry describes bronze 真 as 貝 plus phonetic 𠂈, reports some forms using 鼎 and a 真盤 form adding 丌, and says 貝 and 鼎 may be graphically confused in ancient component use. It reports He Linyi’s proposal that 真 was an early graph for 珍 (‘precious’) and Xie Mingwen’s separate account that 真 was borrowed for ‘true’ and 珍 was later formed with 玉 and 㐱. The entry cites a bronze personal-name use, a Qin Shuihudi legal-question slip for ‘actual/true’, Zhuangzi and Lüshi Chunqiu for ‘inherent nature’, and Xunzi for adverbial ‘indeed’. These distinct uses do not establish a complete chronology or semantic path. The entry does not independently recover the name of an object depicted by 𠂈.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 真

The received Shuowen analysis of 眞 is distinct from competing analyses of the Western Zhou bronze forms.

evidence.source: Historical dictionary text: 說文解字「眞」 and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry parses 眞 through 𠤎, 目, 乚 and 八 and interprets it as an immortal transforming and ascending to heaven. This is a later philological interpretation, not direct evidence for the bronze graph’s original referent or lexical sense.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text with later commentary
evidence.title: 說文解字「眞」

search_audit.query: 真 Western Zhou bronze 真盤 𠂈 phonetic 貝 CUHK 字形
search_audit.outcome: Opened the character-specific entry and inspected its description of bronze components, competing analyses, and cited uses.
Opened the exact Commons file description page and verified its identity, original SVG link, and CC0 statement.

gaps: The supplied local readings for 𠂈 (jié) and 真 (zhēn) are now individually recorded, but their official Unicode character-specific pages were inaccessible in this pass. The readings are modern metadata and do not establish the proposed historical phonetic relation.

No exact artifact image or dated catalogue record was inspected in this pass; the bronze personal-name use and its Western Zhou attribution remain source-reported, and its spoken form and meaning are unidentified.
The earliest word represented by the bronze graph, and the links among ‘true/actual’, ‘inherent nature’, and adverbial ‘indeed’, remain unresolved by the inspected citations.

items.period: Modern reconstruction; not a dated artifact
items.caption: A modern vector reconstruction of 真 in Shuowen seal-script style. Shuowen’s traditional parsing of 眞 differs from competing analyses of the Western Zhou bronze forms.
items.alt: Black seal-script style graph with a tall left stroke, curved upper stroke, rounded central enclosure containing two horizontal bars, and two descending lower strokes.
items.selection_reason: Offers a sourced example of the received seal-script form for comparison with the separately described bronze forms, without presenting the later Shuowen interpretation as settled bronze-era history.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 as stated on the Commons file page.

limitations.text: This is a modern reconstruction, not an ancient artifact image. Its shape and Shuowen parsing do not settle the origin or original meaning of the Western Zhou bronze graph; no image was visually inspected during this research pass.
